readout_other: LFP power and entropy in motor cortex; EMG; time to emergence from propofol anaesthesia
direction_notes: TUS shortened time to emergence from propofol anaesthesia (20.3 min vs 32 min sham) and changed LFP band power (lower at 1-4 and 13-30 Hz, higher at 55-200 Hz) and entropy relative to sham 20 min after TUS.

timing.protocol_description: Stimulation duration, PRF and duty cycle were set as 50 ms, 1 Hz and 5%; the total time for each stimulation was 5 min. The TUS group was stimulated after propofol administration.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Mice were randomly divided into two groups: the Sham group (n = 6) and the TUS group (n = 6).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Twenty-four hours after the surgery, the LFPs and EMG signals were recorded before the administration of propofol. Then, 70  mg/kg propofol (Diprivan, Aspen Pharma Trading Limited, Ireland) was administered by intraperitoneal injection, and the mice in the TUS group were stimulated with low-intensity TUS in the motor cortex after the administration of propofol.

flags.reason: Paper calls 50 ms the 'stimulation duration'; with PRF 1 Hz and duty cycle 5% it is consistent with the pulse duration, so recorded as pulse duration (burst rule resolved by arithmetic).
Pressure 'under the skull' measured by hydrophone 'in the water tank': domain not clear, so placed in unspecified_domain. Transducer is unfocused.
Per-pulse 'stimulation duration' 50 ms vs 5 min total stimulation time; 300 s recorded as the train length.
Figure 7 legend gives n = 12 for the TUS group, inconsistent with 6 per group elsewhere.
